# Superior UI

Produce an interface that belongs to this product. Derive choices from the user's request, existing design evidence, content, and task flow; do not impose a house style or mechanically ban familiar techniques.

## Establish the brief

Before editing, identify:

- the primary user and job this surface supports;
- the content and actions that deserve first attention;
- existing design owners: tokens, typography, components, layouts, brand assets, and documented decisions;
- implementation constraints, affected routes, and states;
- what must remain unchanged.

Inspect the rendered surface when practical. If direction is missing, make the smallest reversible assumption that fits the product and disclose any choice that materially shapes the result.

## Choose a visual thesis

State the direction in one useful sentence, such as “dense operational console with quiet chrome and high-signal status color.” The sentence must constrain actual decisions about hierarchy, density, type, color, shape, or motion. Avoid mood labels that could describe any product.

When the user asks to recreate, match, or closely follow a supplied design, that reference is the visual direction for the requested scope. Do not shortlist alternatives or redesign its visible composition unless the user asks. Read [references/design-recreation.md](references/design-recreation.md) for fidelity, adaptations, and visual verification.

When no governing visual direction exists, shortlist two or three materially different candidates that fit the product and explain each candidate's task fit, defining traits, and principal risk. Select one primary direction before implementation unless the user explicitly requests parallel concepts. A supporting influence may shape a limited detail, but do not blend several named styles into an incoherent trend collage. When a reference's role is ambiguous, preserve its observable characteristics and disclose material assumptions rather than silently redesigning it.

Read [references/visual-system.md](references/visual-system.md) when the task creates a new visual direction, changes several components, needs substantial visual polish, or recreates a design from an image or external reference. Also read [references/style-and-palette-direction.md](references/style-and-palette-direction.md) when selecting among named UI styles, establishing a new palette, or assigning colors to body, component, and typography roles. For focused edits, preserve the local system without loading either reference.

Read [references/reference-source-hygiene.md](references/reference-source-hygiene.md) whenever a screenshot, template, repository, demo, or third-party design materially informs the implementation. Use the reference for source-identity cleanup and for deciding when copied or adapted material requires attribution or license preservation.

Read [references/page-closure-and-footer.md](references/page-closure-and-footer.md) when building or substantially redesigning a landing page, homepage, multi-section marketing page, or footer. Treat the ending as a deliberate part of the page composition without assuming that every site needs a large multi-column footer.

Read [references/semantic-html-and-search-discovery.md](references/semantic-html-and-search-discovery.md) when building or substantially changing a public page whose content must be discoverable, linked, or indexed, including landing pages, homepages, articles, documentation, catalogs, and public detail routes. Keep private dashboards and authenticated tools outside search-oriented requirements unless the product contract says otherwise.

Read [references/expressive-composition-and-component-craft.md](references/expressive-composition-and-component-craft.md) when the direction calls for asymmetric composition, layered depth, editorial tension, or bespoke tactile component details. Use those patterns as candidates justified by content and task—not as mandatory decoration or randomized style selection.

Read [references/motion-and-rendering-performance.md](references/motion-and-rendering-performance.md) when motion is a substantial part of the experience, including animated navigation, overlays, scroll entry, coordinated state transitions, or expressive microinteractions. Keep motion purposeful, accessible, and proportionate to runtime cost.

## Build around the task

- Start with semantic structure and information order; decoration follows.
- Give each region a job. Remove sections that exist only to complete a familiar template when designing freely; for an explicit recreation, preserve the requested reference structure and handle unavailable content honestly.
- Reuse existing primitives when they express the needed hierarchy. Add a variant only when the existing contract cannot.
- Use spacing, type, contrast, alignment, and grouping to create hierarchy before adding containers or effects.
- Let repeated components reflect repeated content. Do not force unlike information into identical cards.
- Keep responsive and accessibility behavior intact. Load the dedicated skills when either concern is a substantial part of the request.

Load `superior-ux` when the primary work is a journey, information architecture, task flow, cross-screen continuity, feedback, or recovery contract. Keep ordinary page hierarchy and visual interaction design here.

## Protect product integrity

Read [references/product-integrity.md](references/product-integrity.md) when the surface includes dashboards, marketing claims, forms, navigation, asynchronous data, or multiple UI states.

At minimum:

- never fabricate metrics, customers, testimonials, activity, compliance, or destinations;
- make controls work, remove them, or label them honestly as unavailable;
- distinguish loading, first-use, filtered-empty, permission-denied, validation, error, and success states when relevant;
- write specific labels and actions using the product's vocabulary;
- preserve user data and existing behavior outside the requested change.

## Critique before delivery

Review the result from three distances:

1. **Page:** Is the primary task obvious, does the composition have intentional rhythm, and does the page end with deliberate visual and informational closure?
2. **Component:** Does each component earn its boundary, emphasis, and interaction?
3. **Detail:** Are labels, icons, states, focus, alignment, and content honest and coherent?

Challenge generic template habits when creating a new direction. In an explicit recreation, the supplied design is evidence for the requested visual choices; do not discard them merely because they resemble a template.

## Verify

Exercise changed interactions and relevant states. Check representative narrow and wide viewports, content extremes, keyboard flow, and the project's normal lint/type/build checks in proportion to the change. For recreation, compare rendered output against the reference at a comparable viewport when practical, iterate on material differences, and report unverified fidelity or necessary deviations. Report concrete results and any unverified risk.

Load `superior-performance` when loading, rendering, responsiveness, bundle cost, or client memory is a primary measured concern. Keep ordinary motion and rendering discipline in this skill when no dedicated performance investigation is needed.

# Superior UX

Make the user's path to a meaningful outcome clear, coherent, and recoverable. Base decisions on product evidence and observable behavior; never invent research, personas, or confidence that the project does not support.

## Establish the experience contract

Before proposing a flow, identify:

- the primary user, job, context, and entry point;
- the successful outcome and how the user recognizes it;
- required decisions, information, permissions, and constraints;
- existing routes, screens, terminology, analytics, research, support evidence, and product rules;
- interruptions, failures, alternate paths, and return visits that materially affect completion.

Separate observed evidence from assumptions. Ask for direction when competing assumptions would change who the product serves, what consent means, or what outcome counts as success. Otherwise, use the smallest reversible assumption and state it.

Read [references/journeys-task-flows-and-information-architecture.md](references/journeys-task-flows-and-information-architecture.md) when work spans multiple steps, screens, roles, entry points, or navigation levels.

## Shape the journey

- Start from the user's goal, not the current screen arrangement or the organization's internal structure.
- Make entry, orientation, next action, progress, completion, and re-entry understandable.
- Distinguish required steps from optional enrichment. Add a step only when it protects comprehension, consent, correctness, or recovery.
- Keep choices comparable and vocabulary stable across surfaces.
- Reveal complexity when it becomes relevant instead of hiding essential consequences or showing every option at once.
- Preserve user control: provide a safe way to go back, cancel, defer, correct, or resume when the product contract allows it.

## Define interaction and recovery

For each consequential action, define what the user can observe before, during, and after it. Cover pending, success, partial success, validation failure, dependency failure, cancellation, and retry only where they can occur.

Read [references/interaction-feedback-and-recovery.md](references/interaction-feedback-and-recovery.md) when the flow contains forms, asynchronous work, destructive actions, external handoffs, interruption, or multi-step state.

Do not optimize completion by concealing cost, consent, security consequences, destructive effects, or meaningful alternatives. Preserve entered data after expected failures when safe, and return the user to a useful state rather than a dead end.

## Evaluate with evidence

Walk through representative scenarios from entry to outcome, including at least one material failure or interruption. Check whether users can answer:

1. Where am I and what can I do here?
2. What will happen if I continue?
3. What is happening now?
4. Did the action succeed, and what should I do next?
5. How do I recover or leave safely?

Read [references/ux-evaluation-and-evidence.md](references/ux-evaluation-and-evidence.md) for heuristic reviews, evidence quality, scenario selection, and usability validation. Describe findings as risks or observed problems at the confidence level the evidence supports; do not present an expert walkthrough as user research.

## Coordinate ownership

Load only the skills whose contracts materially change:

- `superior-ui` for visual hierarchy, component composition, and interface implementation;
- `superior-logic` for domain behavior, state transitions, APIs, and persistence;
- `superior-responsive` for viewport-driven reflow and adaptive navigation;
- `superior-accessibility` for keyboard, focus, semantics, assistive technology, and inclusive interaction;
- `superior-copywriting` for labels, instructions, errors, and product voice;
- `superior-testing` for dedicated journey, contract, or regression test design;
- `superior-docs` when the resulting experience contract must remain durable.

Do not edit implementation when the user asks only for a journey, flow, or review. When implementation is requested, use this skill to govern the experience contract and the owning implementation skills to change code.

## Deliver

Report the current and proposed journey, changed decisions or information structure, interaction and recovery contract, supporting evidence, unresolved assumptions, and validation performed. Prefer a compact flow or state table when sequence or branching would be harder to understand in prose.

# 02 - Use Skills

## Explicit invocation

Prefix a skill name with `$` when you need to ensure that a particular workflow is selected:

```text

```

```text

```

```text

```

Explicit invocation is useful for documentation bootstrapping, audits that must remain read-only, or tasks where neighboring skills could plausibly match.

## Implicit invocation

Codex can select a skill from its description when the request is specific:

```text

```

This request should route to `superior-responsive` without naming it directly.

## Write outcome-oriented prompts

Include:

- the desired result;
- the project area in scope;
- constraints that must be preserved;
- initial evidence or files, when known;
- important verification requirements.

Example:

```text

```

## Avoid

- invoking every skill "just in case";
- using a skill name instead of explaining the objective;
- selecting `superior-ui-audit` when direct implementation is required;
- using `superior-comments` for a change that also modifies executable behavior.

Superior Skills

`superior-skills` is a reusable instruction package for producing software changes that are contextual, evidence-based, and free from a generic template feel. It is not a collection of stylistic prohibitions. Its core principle is to make decisions from project evidence, preserve real functionality, and verify the resulting changes.

## Key differences - Routing is divided by type of work rather than overlapping lists of anti-patterns. - UI creation and UI auditing are separate, preventing implementation requests from turning into read-only audits. - Extensive visual guidance uses progressive disclosure through `references/`. - Each skill has a specific name and description to improve implicit invocation accuracy. - One canonical `skills/` tree serves native plugin and standalone installations across supported coding agents. - Shared baseline rules live in `AGENTS.md`; specialist details are loaded only when relevant. - Agents are instructed to record verified material implementation work in an indexed `docs/implementation-timeline/` by default, with accepted intent and maintenance knowledge curated into existing guides or decisions when useful, unless the user opts out. ## Structure ```text superior-skills/ |-- VERSION |-- CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md |-- CONTRIBUTING.md |-- SECURITY.md |-- LICENSE |-- AGENTS.md |-- CLAUDE.md |-- INSTALL.md |-- plugin.json # Portable Agent Plugin and Antigravity marker |-- gemini-extension.json # Gemini CLI extension |-- kimi.plugin.json # Kimi Code plugin |-- skills/ # Canonical portable skills |-- scripts/ # Package validation |-- .codex-plugin/ # Codex compatibility manifest |-- .cursor-plugin/ # Cursor manifest and repository marketplace |-- .claude-plugin/ # Claude Code manifest and marketplace |-- principles/ | |-- README.md | `-- documentation-continuity.md `-- .agents/ `-- plugins/ # Codex repository marketplace ``` ## Community and governance - [Contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [Security policy](SECURITY.md) - [MIT License](LICENSE) ## Install Superior can be installed as standalone Agent Skills through the Skills CLI or as a portable plugin through a supported host. Plugin installations keep their own cached copy, so refresh the marketplace and start a new session afterward. ### Skills CLI ```shell npx skills update ``` ### Codex ```shell codex plugin marketplace upgrade superior-skills ``` ### Claude Code ```shell claude plugin marketplace update superior-skills claude plugin update superior-skills@superior-skills ``` ### Gemini CLI ```shell gemini extensions update superior-skills ``` Restart Gemini CLI after the extension update. ### Google Antigravity Update the installed plugin through Antigravity's plugin manager. Run `/reload` afterward. ### Cursor Open **Cursor Settings → Plugins**, locate **Superior Skills**, and select the available update or reinstall action. Run **Developer: Reload Window** afterward. Standalone copies do not update automatically; replace the installed `superior-*` skill folders with the latest folders from this repository. ## Usage Skills are selected automatically from the task context or can be invoked explicitly, for example with `$superior-ux`, `$superior-code-review`, `$superior-delivery`, or `$superior-docs`. The portable entrypoint is [`plugin.json`](plugin.json), and canonical skill definitions live under [`skills/`](skills/). ## FAQ ### Does Superior install an MCP server or require credentials? No. Superior is currently a skills-only plugin. It does not install an MCP server, lifecycle hook, credential, or external service. ### Where are the skills installed? Plugin hosts normally install a cached plugin package and read its root `skills/` directory. Standalone hosts instead discover copied skills from their own project or user directories, such as `.agents/skills/`, `.cline/skills/`, or `~/.hermes/skills/`. ### Why is an updated skill not active yet? Refresh or update the marketplace and start a new conversation or agent session. Existing sessions may retain the skill version loaded when the session began. ### Does Superior write implementation documentation automatically? For material, verified implementation work, `superior-docs` instructs the agent to record a focused entry under `docs/implementation-timeline//` in the target project. It may also update a living implementation guide or decision when the current feature contract, criteria, invariants, or safe maintenance path changed. The instructions exclude raw prompts, chat transcripts, and hidden reasoning. An explicit request not to create documentation always takes precedence. Recording depends on the agent loading and following the instructions; Superior does not enforce it with a hook. ### Can I install only one skill? The plugin installs the complete package so routing and shared references remain consistent. For a standalone setup, individual `superior-*` folders can be copied, but any referenced files must be copied with them. ### What happened to `superior-copy`? The copywriting skill is now named `superior-copywriting`. Update explicit `$superior-copy` references to `$superior-copywriting`. If you installed standalone skill folders manually, remove the old `superior-copy` folder and install the new one to avoid duplicate discovery. ## Output principles Superior prioritizes: - local evidence over generic preferences; - hierarchy and task flow before decoration; - honest data and claims; - controls and states that actually work; - accessibility and responsive behavior as part of quality; - small solutions that preserve correctness; - verification proportionate to the risk of the change. The briefs and rationale used to develop the documentation workflow live in `principles/`. That directory is intended for package maintainers; portable runtime instructions live in `skills/superior-docs/`. Explicit user instructions and more specific project rules always take precedence over this package's general preferences.

# Using `superior-accessibility`

This skill handles interface accessibility: semantics, keyboard order, focus, accessible names, contrast, status announcements, and zoom behavior.

## When to use it

Use it when accessibility is requested, required by the product contract, or a changed interaction creates substantial risk: forms, dialogs, composite widgets, navigation, dynamic status, keyboard use, or assistive technology. Do not activate it for every visual edit or use it as a substitute for a general design audit.

## Workflow

1. Identify the affected page, component, and users.
2. Check native semantics before adding ARIA.
3. Review keyboard behavior, focus, labels, status communication, contrast, zoom, and target sizes.
4. For custom or dynamic interactions, verify the complete keyboard, focus, naming, state, and announcement lifecycle.
5. Run available automated checks, then manually validate critical flows.
6. Name the browser, platform, and assistive technology actually tested, and report unavailable combinations.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-accessibility Audit and fix this checkout modal. Ensure focus enters it, is contained correctly, and returns to the trigger afterward.
```

```text
$superior-accessibility Check the registration form for labels, error messages, tab order, contrast, and 200% zoom.
```

## Suitable combinations

- Pair with `superior-ui` when accessibility is part of UI implementation.
- Pair with `superior-responsive` for zoom, reflow, and touch-target issues.
- Pair with `superior-code-review` when accessibility is one risk area in a broader change-set review.
- Pair with `superior-ui-audit` only when the user also requests an accessibility audit; a visual audit does not include it automatically.

## Result checks

Every control should be keyboard-operable, focus should remain visible, control names should be meaningful, and important status changes should be announced. Information must not depend on color alone. Avoid excessive ARIA and do not claim screen-reader compatibility for an environment that was not exercised.

# Using `superior-api-security`

This skill implements or reviews defensive security controls for REST APIs. It covers authentication and authorization boundaries, validation, rate and resource limits, abuse prevention, SSRF, safe errors and logging, and negative security tests.

## When to use it

Use it when security is an explicit part of an endpoint change, for API hardening or review, or when protecting authentication, recovery, payment, reservation, export, webhook, upload, or other sensitive flows. Ordinary API behavior remains owned by `superior-logic`.

## Workflow

1. Map callers, trust boundaries, sensitive resources, operations, and business harm.
2. Trace controls across the gateway, application, identity provider, workers, and downstream services.
3. Select controls for object, function, and property authorization; input and output boundaries; resource cost; automation; outbound requests; and credential lifecycle.
4. For sessions, tokens, reset credentials, API keys, or webhooks, define validation, storage, rotation, revocation, and replay behavior.
5. Implement the smallest coherent control at the authoritative enforcement point.
6. Verify negative cases, lifecycle transitions, limits, failure modes, telemetry, and the deployed-path assumptions.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-api-security Add rate limiting to login and password recovery. Choose keys and thresholds from the current traffic contract, prevent account enumeration, return a stable 429 response, and test concurrent requests.
```

```text
$superior-api-security Review this REST API for cross-tenant object access, mass assignment, unbounded exports, unsafe webhook URLs, and sensitive error disclosure. Implement the confirmed fixes.
```

```text
$superior-api-security Harden this signed webhook flow. Verify the raw payload signature, timestamp window, secret rotation, replay protection, durable acknowledgement, and idempotent duplicate handling.
```

## Suitable combinations

- Pair with `superior-logic` when authorization depends on domain state or the change includes transactions, idempotency, or persistence.
- Pair with `superior-code-review` when security is one risk area in a broader change-set review.
- Pair with `superior-testing` when negative-security fixtures, isolation, or concurrency need dedicated test design.
- Pair with `superior-docs` when the public contract, gateway policy, threat model, or operational procedure changes.
- Pair with `superior-lean` to keep the control proportionate without weakening the identified security requirement.

## Result checks

Credential and webhook work should prove lifecycle, rotation, revocation, and replay behavior at the effective deployed boundary.

Every control should identify its threat, enforcement location, failure behavior, and observable test. Rate limiting should define its keys, allowance, burst, concurrency or cost model, response contract, counter-store behavior, and monitoring—not only install middleware with a default number.

# Using `superior-code-review`

This skill reviews a diff, commit, branch, pull request, or working tree for actionable defects and regressions. It is read-only unless the user explicitly asks for fixes.

## When to use it

Use it when code review is the primary deliverable: review a proposed change, assess merge risk, find regressions, or verify that implementation and tests satisfy an intended contract. Use specialized skills for a dedicated visual, security, database, or performance audit.

## Workflow

1. Confirm the review target, comparison base, intended behavior, and whether fixes are authorized.
2. Read the diff, then trace changed contracts through callers, state, data, configuration, and consumers.
3. Test candidate findings against reachable scenarios and existing protections.
4. Run safe targeted checks that improve confidence.
5. Keep only actionable findings caused or exposed by the target change.
6. Report findings first, ordered by severity, followed by verification and unreviewed risk.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-code-review Review the current branch against main. Focus on correctness, compatibility, and missing regression coverage. Do not modify files.
```

```text
$superior-code-review Review the staged checkout changes. Report only actionable defects with precise file locations, triggers, and consequences.
```

## Suitable combinations

- Pair with `superior-api-security` for an explicitly security-focused review.
- Pair with `superior-database` when migrations, transactions, or stored-data compatibility dominate the risk.
- Pair with `superior-performance` when measured performance analysis is the requested outcome.
- Pair with `superior-testing` when test architecture or reliability needs dedicated review.

## Result checks

A useful review contains a small set of evidenced findings rather than style preferences. It is also valid to report no actionable findings while naming checks performed and material areas that could not be verified.

## Key behaviors:
- Code reviews are read-only by default.
- Do not edit files, submit comments, or approve PRs without an explicit request.
- Findings must include a trigger, a reachable path, concrete consequences, and the precise file location.
- Style preferences and speculative redesigns are not considered defects.
- Findings are prioritized based on impact and scope.
- A result of "no actionable findings" is considered valid.
- A general review does not automatically evolve into a security audit, visual audit, or implementation task.

# Using `superior-comments`

This skill refines code comments without changing executable behavior. Valuable comments explain rationale, invariants, risks, contracts, or workarounds that are not apparent from the code.

## When to use it

Use it to audit comments, remove narration that only repeats code, improve TODOs, or preserve security and legal context. Do not use it for refactoring, symbol renaming, whole-file formatting, or logic changes.

## Workflow

1. Define the files or directories that may be touched.
2. Distinguish high-value comments from decorative, stale, or purely narrational ones.
3. Edit comments only; preserve code, unrelated whitespace, and behavior.
4. Review the diff to confirm that every change is comment-only.
5. Run lightweight checks when comment formatting affects tooling.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-comments Audit comments in src/auth/. Preserve security rationale and remove comments that merely repeat the code.
```

```text
$superior-comments Refine TODOs in this file so each one has a clear action or completion condition. Do not change the code.
```

## Suitable combinations

This skill is usually best used alone so the comment-only boundary remains easy to verify. After a substantial `superior-logic` change, run it as a separate task if comments also need synchronization.

## Result checks

The diff should contain comments only. Every remaining comment should add information that is not obvious from the implementation. Do not remove security, licensing, legal, invariant, or workaround notes without evidence that they are obsolete.

# Using `superior-database`

This skill handles database work where schema, query, transaction, migration, or data-lifecycle decisions materially affect correctness or rollout safety.

## When to use it

Use it for schema and index design, query correctness, transaction boundaries, concurrency controls, production-facing migrations, backfills, data repair, or datastore review. Routine repository calls with unchanged data contracts remain under `superior-logic`.

## Workflow

1. Identify the datastore engine, version, schema authority, data ownership, and compatibility window.
2. Establish invariants, access patterns, cardinality, volume, and concurrency behavior.
3. Design schema, queries, indexes, and transaction boundaries as one contract.
4. Plan compatibility-first rollout, verification, and recovery before migration execution.
5. Test with the real engine and representative state when engine semantics or scale owns the risk.
6. Report the environment, data scale, commands, results, and unverified rollout conditions.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-database Add tenant-scoped uniqueness for user email without blocking existing reads. Inspect legacy duplicates, plan a compatible migration, and define verification before enforcing the constraint.
```

```text
$superior-database Review this order-creation transaction for duplicate delivery and concurrent inventory updates. Preserve the existing database and migration tooling.
```

## Suitable combinations

- Pair with `superior-logic` for the application behavior that consumes the data contract.
- Pair with `superior-testing` for migration, compatibility, integration, or concurrency test design.
- Pair with `superior-api-security` for tenant isolation, query injection, or sensitive-data boundaries.
- Pair with `superior-debugging` when the data symptom's cause is not established.

## Result checks

A useful result proves data integrity and compatibility, names lock and recovery risks, and distinguishes locally verified behavior from production rollout safety. A generated migration file alone is not sufficient evidence.

## Key capabilities include:
- defining schemas, constraints, queries, and indexes based on actual access patterns;
- managing transaction isolation, locking, concurrency, idempotency, replication, caching, and event consistency;
- executing rollout migrations through expand, migrate, verify, and contract phases;
- performing backfills that are bounded, resumable, observable, and safe to re-run;
- evaluating the impact of locks, table rewrites, replication lag, recovery processes, and compatibility windows;
- prohibiting the execution of production migrations or destructive queries without explicit targeting and authorization.

# Using `superior-debugging`

This skill investigates a concrete software failure when the cause is uncertain, then repairs the boundary that owns the violated contract.

## When to use it

Use it for reproducible bugs, intermittent failures, environment-specific behavior, production incidents with available evidence, or proposed fixes whose causal basis is unclear. Do not invoke it for feature work, general code review, or speculative cleanup without an observed failure.

## Workflow

1. Define expected and observed behavior from authoritative evidence.
2. Establish the smallest reproduction, affected scope, and last-known-good state when available.
3. Separate symptom, trigger, root cause, and amplifiers.
4. Test falsifiable hypotheses with the cheapest safe discriminating checks.
5. Repair the boundary that owns the broken contract.
6. Re-run the original reproduction and verify relevant neighboring behavior.
7. Report confidence and unresolved environmental or operational uncertainty.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-debugging Diagnose why duplicate invoices are created only when the payment webhook is retried. Trace the persisted state and queue delivery before proposing a repair.
```

```text
$superior-debugging Investigate this production-only timeout using the available sanitized traces and configuration. Do not change production settings or increase the timeout without proving the causal mechanism.
```

## Suitable combinations

- Pair with `superior-logic` when the confirmed repair changes application behavior or persistence.
- Pair with `superior-testing` when regression coverage or nondeterministic test behavior needs dedicated design.
- Pair with `superior-api-security` when the failure exposes a security control weakness.

## Result checks

A useful result distinguishes observations from hypotheses, explains the causal chain, verifies the original symptom, and labels remaining uncertainty. A restart, retry, timeout increase, or disappearing error alone is not proof of resolution.

A useful result distinguishes build, package, publication, deployment, and promotion. It identifies the immutable artifact and source revision, records every external mutation, and does not claim rollout or rollback behavior that was not exercised.

# Using `superior-docs`

This skill maintains curated project memory across sessions. Its six primary modes are Bootstrap, Record, Memory, Synchronize, Reconstruct, and Handoff.

## Choose the right mode

- **Bootstrap**: establish a documentation foundation for a project that does not have one.
- **Record**: automatically capture a verified material implementation outcome unless the user opts out.
- **Memory**: curate accepted intent, criteria, decisions, and maintenance knowledge without preserving raw prompts or chat history.
- **Synchronize**: align documentation after implementation changes.
- **Reconstruct**: recover context from code and distributed evidence.
- **Handoff**: record work status, decisions, risks, and next steps.

Keep current facts, accepted decisions, history, plans, and unknowns separate. Do not present plans as implemented state.

## Workflow

1. State the mode and project scope.
2. Read relevant code, configuration, tests, documentation, repository status, and the task's final diff as evidence.
3. For implementation work, create or update the outcome record in `docs/implementation-timeline/<feature-domain>/` with a specific dated filename and maintain the root and domain indexes.
4. Curate accepted intent, criteria, scope, and maintenance notes when they add durable context. Update an implementation guide only when its living contract or safe modification path changed.
5. Update the core documents in `docs/structure-of-app/` only when their current-state claims changed.
6. Create other specialized directories only when supported by evidence and a real need.
7. Validate links, terminology, implementation status, task attribution, and potential secret exposure.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-docs Bootstrap documentation for this project from the existing code. Mark uncertainty and do not invent decisions.
```

```text
$superior-docs Synchronize documentation after the authentication-flow changes on this branch.
```

```text
$superior-docs Curate the accepted requirements and verified implementation of this feature into durable project memory. Do not store the raw conversation.
```

## Suitable combinations

Use it automatically after `superior-ui`, `superior-logic`, or another skill produces a verified material implementation change. The user may explicitly opt out for the task. For complete procedures, continue to [documentation bootstrapping](../../04-bootstrap-project-docs.md), [new sessions](../../05-start-a-new-session.md), and [maintenance](../../06-maintain-project-docs.md).

## Result checks

Documentation should be traceable to evidence, navigable from its index, and honest about unknowns. In a dirty worktree, do not attribute pre-existing or concurrent user changes to the current task. Do not copy entire implementations into docs or create empty directories merely to decorate the structure.

# Using `superior-lean`

This skill seeks the smallest solution that remains complete, correct, safe, and contract-compliant. Its routing and runtime instructions are owned entirely by Superior.

## When to use it

Use it when an implementation is accumulating abstractions, dependencies, wrappers, configuration, or layers that may not be justified. Do not use it to remove user requirements, security, accessibility, compatibility, or concurrency protections.

## Workflow

1. State the contract that must be fulfilled and the risks that cannot be ignored.
2. Look for existing capabilities in local code, the standard library, the native platform, or installed dependencies.
3. Compare solutions by the number of new concepts, not merely lines of code.
4. Distinguish accidental machinery from boundaries justified by current consumers, external systems, policy, compatibility, or real variation.
5. Trace indirect consumers and compare total ownership before removing shared code or dependencies.
6. Test important behavior and explain the remaining trade-offs.

Code with no direct callers may still be activated through registries, configuration, routes, events, reflection, build tooling, or public APIs. Likewise, a dependency is simpler to remove only when the project can safely own its complete behavior and maintenance burden—not merely reproduce its happy path in fewer lines.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-lean Implement this simple cache using existing capabilities. Avoid a new dependency unless it is genuinely necessary.
```

```text
$superior-lean Review and simplify this design without weakening validation, security, or retry behavior.
```

## Suitable combinations

- Pair with `superior-logic` to keep backend changes small but robust.
- Pair with `superior-ui` to avoid speculative components and variants.
- Pair with `superior-docs` when simplification changes a documented architectural decision.

## Result checks

The final solution should satisfy every acceptance criterion while introducing as few new concepts as practical. Ensure that simplicity did not come from removing required error handling, validation, observability, or in-scope edge cases.

# Using `superior-performance`

This skill investigates and improves performance when latency, throughput, resource use, loading, rendering, bundle cost, or capacity is a primary concern.

## When to use it

Use it for a measured slowdown, accepted performance budget, capacity limit, expensive workload, client loading or interaction problem, or a performance-focused review. Do not use it for speculative micro-optimization without a symptom, target, or demonstrated bottleneck.

## Workflow

1. Define the affected journey, workload, metric, target, and non-negotiable correctness constraints.
2. Capture a repeatable baseline with the environment, data shape, concurrency, and cache state.
3. Profile the representative workload and identify the owning bottleneck.
4. Remove unnecessary work or optimize the constrained resource without shifting hidden cost elsewhere.
5. Repeat the same measurement protocol and run correctness checks.
6. Report before/after evidence, variance, tradeoffs, and untested conditions.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-performance Reduce the p95 latency of this export path. First reproduce it with representative row counts, profile database, serialization, and transfer time, then optimize only the dominant contributor.
```

```text
$superior-performance Investigate slow interaction on the mobile catalog route. Use the existing browser tooling, preserve accessibility, and compare loading and input responsiveness before and after.
```

## Suitable combinations

- Pair with `superior-debugging` when the cause of the slowdown is uncertain.
- Pair with `superior-database` when query plans, indexes, locks, or datastore capacity owns the cost.
- Pair with `superior-testing` for reliable benchmark or performance-regression automation.
- Pair with interface skills when the optimization changes rendering, interaction, responsive behavior, or accessibility.

## Result checks

A useful result includes comparable before/after evidence, workload and environment details, correctness checks, and resource or cost tradeoffs. An isolated faster run within normal variance is inconclusive.

## Key principles:
- There must be a measurable symptom, target, budget, or bottleneck.
- Compare conditions before and after, using the same workload.
- Use evidence such as profiles, traces, query plans, allocations, or browser timelines.
- Reject speculative micro-optimization.
- Do not consider a single faster execution as proof.
- Maintain correctness, security, accessibility, backpressure, and boundedness.
- Treat caching, concurrency, lazy loading, and preloading as tradeoffs, not as automatic solutions.
- Production activities—such as profiling, load generation, and cache flushing—always require explicit authorization.

3. Prioritize failure modes by impact, reach, detection delay, and recovery difficulty.
4. Add bounded timeout, retry, isolation, degradation, backpressure, or redundancy only where evidence justifies it.

6. Verify failure and recovery in the narrowest authorized environment that preserves the mechanism.


```text

```

- Pair with `superior-performance` for capacity and saturation measurement.

A useful result names the objective, failure mode, blast radius, control owner, degradation behavior, detection, recovery, and residual risk. Configuration review alone does not prove high availability, backup restoration, failover, or disaster recovery.

# Using `superior-responsive`

This skill improves how interfaces adapt to available space: reflow, overflow, navigation, content order, content-driven breakpoints, zoom, and touch targets.

## When to use it

Use it when layouts break, content is clipped, tables become unusable, navigation grows crowded, or components are merely scaled down instead of recomposed. Do not use it for a broad visual redesign when responsiveness is not the primary problem.

## Workflow

1. Reproduce the failure with realistic viewports and content.
2. Find the owner of the width, overflow, min-content, or constraint causing the problem.
3. Recompose according to content priority instead of shrinking everything, while preserving one authoritative semantic and source hierarchy.
4. Introduce local scrolling only where it is intentional.
5. When runtime space changes, account for the visual viewport, virtual keyboard, safe areas, orientation, input capability, and embedded container.
6. Test wide, near-breakpoint, and narrow viewports, as well as zoom, long text, touch, and keyboard use.

For new or multi-region layouts, the skill can define distinct desktop and mobile compositions while preserving the same task contract. It selects among patterns such as split-to-stack, sidebar-to-drawer, grid-to-list, table-to-scroller or alternate representation, mega-navigation-to-disclosure, and multi-column-footer-to-prioritized groups.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-responsive Fix this dashboard between 320px and 768px. Prioritize reflow and do not hide the primary action.
```

```text
$superior-responsive Keep the transaction table usable on mobile with local scrolling and clear headers.
```

```text
$superior-responsive Design coordinated desktop and mobile compositions for this account page. Preserve actions and content, but do not treat mobile as a scaled-down desktop.
```

## Suitable combinations

- Pair with `superior-ui` when building or redesigning a page.
- Pair with `superior-accessibility` for zoom, keyboard, reading order, and target size.
- Pair with `superior-performance` when client loading, rendering, or responsiveness requires measurement and profiling.
- Pair with `superior-copywriting` when realistic text length is part of layout testing.

## Result checks

The page should not scroll horizontally unless explicitly intended. Important content must remain available, touch targets must remain usable, and reading and focus order must make sense. Breakpoints should respond to content needs rather than customary device numbers. Width-only emulation is insufficient when keyboards, safe areas, orientation, or touch behavior own the risk.

# Using `superior-testing`

This skill designs, implements, repairs, or reviews automated tests when testing itself requires dedicated decisions about risk, test level, isolation, fixtures, or reliability.

## When to use it

Use it for regression tests, test strategy, missing coverage at an important boundary, flaky failures, contract tests, or a substantial test-suite change. Do not invoke it merely because an ordinary implementation should run existing checks before delivery.

## Workflow

1. Identify the observable contract, regression, and risk being protected.
2. Inspect existing test tools, conventions, fixtures, and CI constraints.
3. Choose the narrowest test level that exercises the real owner of the risk.
4. Make state, time, randomness, concurrency, and external boundaries deterministic where the test owns them.
5. Run the focused test first, then the relevant neighboring suite and repository checks.
6. Report what was proved and which environments or conditions remain untested.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-testing Add regression coverage for duplicate webhook delivery. Prove that retries cannot create a second payment without mocking the idempotency store.
```

```text
$superior-testing Diagnose and repair this flaky asynchronous test. Identify the uncontrolled condition instead of adding retries or a larger timeout.
```

## Suitable combinations

- Pair with `superior-logic` when production business behavior or state transitions also change.
- Pair with `superior-api-security` for negative authorization, limiter, token, SSRF, or abuse-control verification.
- Pair with an interface skill when component, accessibility, responsive, or interaction behavior owns the asserted contract.

## Result checks

A useful result explains the protected contract, why the selected level is credible, which command passed or failed, and what risk remains. Coverage percentage alone is not evidence that the important behavior was tested.

## Key characteristics of the skill:
- Active when testing constitutes a core part of the work.
- Encompasses regression testing, test strategy, contract testing, fixtures, mocks/doubles, flaky tests, concurrency, timing, and external systems.
- Goes beyond simply executing existing tests as part of routine implementation.
- Does not impose specific frameworks, a rigid "test pyramid," or generic coverage targets.
- Prioritizes the smallest possible test level that effectively addresses the relevant risks.

# Using `superior-ui-audit`

This skill performs read-only visual audits. Its output is a small set of strong, prioritized findings with clear correction paths, not direct code changes.

## When to use it

Use it to assess an existing interface before redesign or implementation. Do not use it when the user directly requests code changes. Functional and accessibility problems remain out of scope unless explicitly requested.

## Workflow

1. Establish the pages, viewports, states, and visual evidence to assess.
2. For each candidate finding, require an observation, a violated contract or design expectation, a causal connection, and an actionable correction.
3. Prioritize by impact on user tasks, hierarchy, clarity, and consistency.
4. Limit the report to the five strongest findings.
5. Keep any implementation plan optional and do not edit files.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-ui-audit Audit this checkout page as read-only work. Report no more than five major visual issues with specific corrections.
```

```text
$superior-ui-audit Compare this dashboard with the project's design system. Do not change code or assess the backend.
```

## Suitable combinations

Run the audit as a separate stage before `superior-ui`. Add `superior-accessibility` or `superior-responsive` scope only when requested, and clearly identify which findings come from the additional scope.

## Result checks

The report should not become a long list of subjective preferences. Every finding must be demonstrable from the interface and connected to user impact. Confirm that no files changed during the audit.

# Using `superior-ui`

This skill builds, redesigns, or refines product interfaces using project evidence, realistic content, functional states, and deliberate visual composition.

## When to use it

Use it to implement pages, components, dashboards, product flows, or redesigns that require UI code changes. Use `superior-ui-audit` for read-only reports and `superior-logic` for nonvisual behavior changes.

## Workflow

1. Study the users, primary tasks, design owners, components, tokens, and existing patterns.
2. Establish a visual thesis and hierarchy before adding decorative details.
3. Build with semantic structure, realistic content, and loading, empty, error, and success states.
4. Ensure controls actually work and connect to the intended behavior.
5. Critique the result at page, component, and detail levels, then test primary interactions and viewports.

When the project has no governing visual direction, the skill can shortlist two or three suitable styles, explain their fit and risks, and select one primary direction before implementation. Color references are mapped to semantic body, component, typography, interaction, and state tokens; palette order alone does not determine usage.

For design recreation, screenshots provide hierarchy and proportion rather than trustworthy CSS measurements. The skill checks existing typography tokens first; when none exist, it starts from readable body, control, and caption baselines and adjusts them against the rendered result instead of reproducing tiny apparent pixels.

For landing pages and homepages, the skill also treats the footer as deliberate page closure. It selects a minimal utility, sitemap, conversion, editorial, or product-service mode from real routes and content instead of defaulting every design to a thin generic strip or inventing links to fill columns.

For public pages that must be discovered or indexed, the skill preserves a meaningful HTML hierarchy, stable source order, crawlable navigation, route-owned metadata, and the project's established rendering strategy. These requirements do not apply automatically to private dashboards or authenticated tools.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-ui Build a team settings page that follows the existing design system. Include loading, empty, error, and success states.
```

```text
$superior-ui Redesign this dashboard to clarify its decision hierarchy without changing the API contract.
```

## Suitable combinations

- Add `superior-responsive` for adaptation across sizes.
- Add `superior-ux` when journeys, information architecture, task flows, feedback, or recovery are primary.
- Add `superior-accessibility` for deeper accessibility checks.
- Add `superior-copywriting` when product text is also being designed.
- Add `superior-logic` when APIs or application behavior also change.
- Use `superior-docs` after a durable change that alters project context.

## Result checks

The interface should fit the product rather than resemble a generic template. Its hierarchy, content, states, and interactions should be complete. Preserve the existing design system where applicable, and do not invent data, features, or social proof.

# Using `superior-ux`

This skill designs or reviews how users understand and complete a goal across steps or surfaces. It owns journeys, information architecture, task flows, feedback, recovery, and cross-screen continuity.

## When to use it

Use it when the main question is how a product experience should work from entry to outcome: onboarding, checkout, authentication, multi-step forms, navigation structure, approval flows, empty-to-active journeys, or recovery after interruption. Use `superior-ui` when visual implementation is primary and `superior-logic` when the task is only about application behavior.

## Workflow

1. Identify the user, job, context, entry point, successful outcome, and available evidence.
2. Map required decisions, steps, alternate paths, interruptions, and re-entry.
3. Organize information around user decisions rather than internal teams or data structures.
4. Define observable pending, success, failure, cancellation, and recovery behavior where relevant.
5. Walk representative scenarios and report evidence, assumptions, unresolved risks, and validation.

The skill does not invent personas, research findings, or usability claims. When evidence is limited, it labels the proposed experience as a hypothesis and explains how to validate it.

## Prompt examples

```text
$superior-ux Review the account recovery journey from sign-in failure to restored access. Identify dead ends, unclear decisions, and missing recovery states without changing code.
```

```text
$superior-ux $superior-ui Redesign onboarding so a new workspace can reach its first successful import with fewer ambiguous decisions. Preserve required consent and security steps.
```

## Suitable combinations

- Add `superior-ui` for visual hierarchy, components, and interface implementation.
- Add `superior-logic` when state transitions, APIs, or persistence change.
- Add `superior-responsive` when the journey changes across viewport sizes.
- Add `superior-accessibility` for keyboard, focus, semantics, and assistive technology.
- Add `superior-copywriting` when labels, instructions, and error messages need dedicated work.
- Add `superior-testing` for substantial journey or regression test design.

## Result checks

The result should make entry, orientation, decisions, progress, completion, interruption, and recovery explicit. Each recommendation should connect to evidence or a clearly labeled assumption, and implementation ownership should remain with the relevant UI, logic, responsive, accessibility, copy, or testing skill.

# Menggunakan `superior-api-security`

Skill ini menerapkan atau meninjau kontrol keamanan defensif untuk REST API. Cakupannya meliputi boundary autentikasi dan otorisasi, validasi, pembatasan rate dan resource, pencegahan abuse, SSRF, error dan logging yang aman, serta negative security test.

## Kapan dipakai

Gunakan ketika keamanan menjadi bagian eksplisit dari perubahan endpoint, saat melakukan hardening atau review API, atau ketika melindungi login, recovery, pembayaran, reservasi, export, webhook, upload, dan flow sensitif lain. Perilaku API biasa tetap menjadi tanggung jawab `superior-logic`.

## Alur kerja

1. Petakan caller, trust boundary, resource sensitif, operasi, dan dampak bisnis.
2. Telusuri kontrol pada gateway, aplikasi, identity provider, worker, dan downstream service.
3. Pilih kontrol untuk otorisasi object/function/property, boundary input-output, biaya resource, otomatisasi, outbound request, dan lifecycle credential.
4. Untuk session, token, reset credential, API key, atau webhook, tentukan validation, storage, rotation, revocation, dan replay behavior.
5. Terapkan kontrol koheren yang paling kecil pada enforcement point yang berwenang.
6. Verifikasi negative case, lifecycle transition, limit, failure mode, telemetry, dan asumsi pada deployment path.

## Contoh prompt

```text
$superior-api-security Tambahkan rate limiting pada login dan password recovery. Tentukan key serta threshold dari kontrak traffic saat ini, cegah account enumeration, kembalikan respons 429 yang stabil, dan uji concurrent request.
```

```text
$superior-api-security Tinjau REST API ini untuk cross-tenant object access, mass assignment, export tanpa batas, URL webhook yang tidak aman, dan kebocoran detail melalui error. Implementasikan perbaikan yang terkonfirmasi.
```

```text

```

## Kombinasi yang sesuai

- Dengan `superior-logic` ketika otorisasi bergantung pada state domain atau perubahan mencakup transaksi, idempotency, dan persistence.
- Dengan `superior-code-review` ketika security merupakan salah satu risiko dalam review change set yang lebih luas.

## Hasil yang perlu diperiksa

Pekerjaan credential dan webhook harus membuktikan lifecycle, rotation, revocation, dan replay pada deployed boundary yang efektif.

Setiap kontrol harus memiliki ancaman, lokasi enforcement, perilaku saat gagal, dan pengujian yang dapat diamati. Rate limiting perlu mendefinisikan key, allowance, burst, concurrency atau cost model, kontrak respons, perilaku counter store, dan monitoring—bukan hanya memasang middleware dengan angka default.

# Menggunakan `superior-docs`

Skill ini memelihara memori proyek yang telah dikurasi dan tahan lintas sesi. Enam mode utamanya adalah Bootstrap, Record, Memory, Synchronize, Reconstruct, dan Handoff.

## Pilih mode yang tepat

- **Bootstrap**: membuat fondasi docs untuk proyek yang belum memilikinya.
- **Record**: mencatat otomatis outcome implementasi material yang telah diverifikasi kecuali pengguna menolaknya.
- **Memory**: mengkurasi intent, criteria, decision, dan pengetahuan maintenance yang telah diterima tanpa menyimpan prompt mentah atau riwayat chat.
- **Synchronize**: menyelaraskan docs setelah perubahan implementasi.
- **Reconstruct**: membangun kembali konteks dari kode dan bukti yang tersebar.
- **Handoff**: mencatat status kerja, keputusan, risiko, dan langkah berikutnya.

Pisahkan fakta saat ini, keputusan yang diterima, riwayat, rencana, dan hal yang belum diketahui. Jangan menyajikan rencana sebagai keadaan implementasi.

## Alur kerja

1. Nyatakan mode dan cakupan proyek.
2. Baca kode, konfigurasi, tes, docs, status repository, dan diff final tugas sebagai bukti.
3. Untuk pekerjaan implementasi, buat atau perbarui catatan outcome di `docs/implementation-timeline/<feature-domain>/` dengan nama file bertanggal yang spesifik, lalu pelihara indeks root dan domainnya.
4. Kurasi intent, criteria, scope, dan maintenance notes yang telah diterima jika menambah konteks durable. Perbarui implementation guide hanya ketika living contract atau jalur perubahan amannya berubah.
5. Perbarui dokumen inti di `docs/structure-of-app/` hanya ketika klaim current-state berubah.
6. Buat folder khusus lain hanya jika ada bukti dan kebutuhan nyata.
7. Validasi tautan, istilah, status implementasi, atribusi tugas, dan kebocoran secret.

## Contoh prompt

```text
$superior-docs Bootstrap dokumentasi proyek ini dari kode yang ada. Tandai ketidakpastian dan jangan mengarang keputusan.
```

```text
$superior-docs Synchronize docs setelah perubahan alur autentikasi pada branch ini.
```

```text
$superior-docs Kurasi requirement yang diterima dan implementasi fitur yang telah diverifikasi menjadi memori proyek durable. Jangan simpan percakapan mentah.
```

## Kombinasi yang sesuai

Gunakan secara otomatis setelah `superior-ui`, `superior-logic`, atau skill lain menghasilkan perubahan implementasi material yang telah diverifikasi. Pengguna dapat menolak dokumentasi secara eksplisit untuk tugas tersebut. Untuk prosedur lengkap, lanjutkan ke [bootstrap docs](../../04-bootstrap-project-docs.md), [sesi baru](../../05-start-a-new-session.md), dan [maintenance](../../06-maintain-project-docs.md).

## Hasil yang perlu diperiksa

Dokumentasi harus dapat ditelusuri ke bukti, mudah dinavigasi dari indeks, dan jujur mengenai unknown. Pada dirty worktree, jangan mengatribusikan perubahan lama atau concurrent milik pengguna kepada tugas saat ini. Jangan menyalin seluruh kode ke docs atau membuat folder kosong sebagai hiasan struktur.

- Menolak micro-optimization spekulatif.
- Tidak menganggap satu eksekusi yang lebih cepat sebagai bukti.
- Mempertahankan correctness, security, accessibility, backpressure, dan boundedness.
- Memperlakukan cache, concurrency, lazy loading, dan preloading sebagai tradeoff, bukan solusi otomatis.

Gunakan `superior-ui` bila implementasi visual menjadi concern utama dan `superior-logic` bila tugas hanya membahas behavior aplikasi.

## Alur kerja

1. Identifikasi pengguna, pekerjaan, konteks, entry point, outcome sukses, dan evidence yang tersedia.
2. Petakan keputusan wajib, langkah, jalur alternatif, interupsi, dan re-entry.
3. Susun informasi berdasarkan keputusan pengguna, bukan tim internal atau struktur data.
4. Tentukan behavior pending, success, failure, cancellation, dan recovery yang dapat diamati bila relevan.
5. Jalankan walkthrough skenario representatif lalu laporkan evidence, asumsi, risiko yang belum terjawab, dan validasi.

Skill tidak mengarang persona, temuan riset, atau klaim usability. Bila evidence terbatas, rancangan experience dinyatakan sebagai hipotesis beserta cara memvalidasinya.

## Contoh prompt

```text
$superior-ux Tinjau journey pemulihan akun dari kegagalan sign-in hingga akses pulih. Temukan dead end, keputusan yang tidak jelas, dan recovery state yang hilang tanpa mengubah kode.
```

```text
$superior-ux $superior-ui Redesign onboarding agar workspace baru dapat mencapai import pertama yang sukses dengan lebih sedikit keputusan ambigu. Pertahankan langkah consent dan keamanan yang wajib.
```

## Kombinasi yang sesuai

- Tambahkan `superior-ui` untuk hierarki visual, komponen, dan implementasi interface.
- Tambahkan `superior-logic` bila state transition, API, atau persistence berubah.
- Tambahkan `superior-responsive` bila journey berubah pada ukuran viewport berbeda.
- Tambahkan `superior-accessibility` untuk keyboard, fokus, semantik, dan assistive technology.
- Tambahkan `superior-copywriting` bila label, instruksi, dan pesan error memerlukan pekerjaan khusus.
- Tambahkan `superior-testing` untuk desain journey test atau regression test yang substansial.

## Hasil yang perlu diperiksa

Hasil harus memperjelas entry, orientation, decision, progress, completion, interruption, dan recovery. Setiap rekomendasi harus terhubung pada evidence atau asumsi yang diberi label dengan jelas, sedangkan kepemilikan implementasi tetap berada pada skill UI, logic, responsive, accessibility, copy, atau testing yang relevan.

# Installing Superior Skills

Superior Skills is a skills-only portable Agent Plugin. It does not install an MCP server, lifecycle hooks, credentials, or external services.

## Package layout

- `plugin.json` is the portable entrypoint used by Agent Plugin-compatible hosts and the root marker used by Antigravity plugins.
- `gemini-extension.json` is the native Gemini CLI extension manifest.
- `kimi.plugin.json` is the native Kimi Code plugin manifest.
- `skills/` contains the canonical skill definitions.
- `.codex-plugin/`, `.cursor-plugin/`, and `.claude-plugin/` provide host-specific compatibility and marketplace metadata.
- `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` exposes the package to a repository-scoped Codex marketplace.

## Skills CLI (skills.sh)

With Node.js and npm available, install Superior Skills directly into a supported agent through the [Skills CLI](https://www.skills.sh/docs/cli):

```shell
npx skills add KodekaTeam/superior-skills
```

The interactive flow lets you select individual skills, target agents, and project or global scope. Project scope is the default. To make the selected skills available across projects, use:

```shell
npx skills add KodekaTeam/superior-skills -g
```

This installs standalone skills into the selected agent directories. It does not install the host-specific plugin manifests or marketplace entry described below.

## Codex and ChatGPT Work

Add the GitHub repository as a Codex marketplace, then install the plugin:

```shell
codex plugin marketplace add KodekaTeam/superior-skills
codex plugin add superior-skills@superior-skills
```

For repository-local development, clone or copy the package into a trusted repository and keep `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` at that repository root. The marketplace exposes the package at `./` as `superior-skills`.

In supported Codex clients, refresh the plugin marketplace, select **Superior Skills**, and install it. The root portable manifest and `skills/` directory are the canonical package content.

For a direct project installation without the plugin marketplace, create `.agents/skills/` in the target repository and copy every folder from this package's root `skills/` directory into it. Copy or merge `AGENTS.md` separately:

```text
project/
|-- AGENTS.md
`-- .agents/
    `-- skills/
        `-- superior-*/
```

If the project already has `AGENTS.md`, merge the portable baseline without removing project-specific commands, architecture, domain rules, or nested instruction boundaries.

## Cursor

For a Git-backed installation:

1. Open **Cursor Settings → Plugins**.
2. Paste `https://github.com/KodekaTeam/superior-skills` into the plugin search box.
3. Open **Superior Skills** and select **Install**.
4. Run **Developer: Reload Window** before testing the installed skills.

For local testing:

1. Copy this complete package directory to `~/.cursor/plugins/local/superior-skills/`.
2. Restart Cursor or run **Developer: Reload Window**.
3. Open **Customize**, locate **Superior Skills**, and confirm the packaged skills are listed.

Do not use a symlink to a directory outside `~/.cursor/plugins/local`; Cursor restricts those local plugin symlinks. For team repository import, use the included `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json` from the repository root.

## Claude Code

For a Git-backed marketplace installation, run these commands inside Claude Code:

```text
/plugin marketplace add KodekaTeam/superior-skills
/plugin install superior-skills@superior-skills
```

During local development, load the package directory directly:

```text
claude --plugin-dir /absolute/path/to/superior-skills
```

Plugin skills are namespaced in Claude Code, for example:

```text
/superior-skills:superior-ui
/superior-skills:superior-api-security
/superior-skills:superior-docs
```

`CLAUDE.md` is the project-maintenance baseline for contributors working in this repository. Plugin-installed skills remain on demand.

## Gemini CLI

Install Superior Skills as a native extension from GitHub:

```shell
gemini extensions install https://github.com/KodekaTeam/superior-skills
```

Restart Gemini CLI, then confirm discovery with:

```text
/skills list
```

For local development without reinstalling after every edit, link the repository directory:

```shell
gemini extensions link /absolute/path/to/superior-skills
```

The extension loads the canonical root `skills/` directory. It does not add MCP servers, hooks, settings, or credentials.

## Google Antigravity

Antigravity CLI can install the complete repository as a plugin bundle:

```shell
agy plugin install https://github.com/KodekaTeam/superior-skills
agy plugin list
```

For Antigravity IDE, copy the complete package directory to one of the supported plugin locations:

- workspace: `<workspace>/.agents/plugins/superior-skills/`;
- global: `~/.gemini/config/plugins/superior-skills/`.

Keep `plugin.json` and `skills/` together at the plugin root. Antigravity also supports standalone workspace skills under `.agents/skills/` when the complete plugin is not required.

## Kimi Code

From the Kimi Code TUI, install the repository through the custom plugin flow:

```text

/plugins info superior-skills
/reload
```

Kimi copies the installed repository into its managed plugin store. Editing the original checkout does not update that managed copy; reinstall or use the plugin manager's update action after local changes.

## Cline

Use Skills CLI and select Cline as the target:

```shell
npx skills add KodekaTeam/superior-skills
```

For a manual installation, copy selected `skills/superior-*` directories into `.cline/skills/` for workspace scope or `~/.cline/skills/` for user scope. Keep every referenced file inside each copied skill directory. Start a new conversation or reload the editor after installation.

## Muse Code

Muse Code reads project skills from `.agents/skills/` and personal skills from `~/.agents/skills/`. Copy selected canonical skill directories into the appropriate location.

If Superior Skills is already installed in a Codex user skill directory, Muse can import that installation:

```shell

```

Use `muse skills list` to confirm discovery. A Muse-specific plugin manifest is intentionally not included because the package is skills-only and Muse already imports or discovers the canonical skill directories.

## Hermes Agent

Hermes integrates with the skills.sh catalog. Search, inspect, and install the required Superior skills individually:

```shell
hermes skills search superior --source skills-sh
hermes skills inspect <result-id>
hermes skills install <result-id>
```

Use the exact identifier returned by the search command. Run `hermes skills list` afterward to confirm installation. Individual installation preserves progressive disclosure and avoids loading unrelated skills.

## User-scoped standalone skills

When a host supports standalone Agent Skills but not plugin installation, copy each folder under `skills/` to that host's user skill directory. Host-specific instruction files must be merged separately; do not blindly replace an existing `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`.

```shell

```

The CLI lets you choose the applicable project or global scope. Start a new agent session after the update.

### Codex

```shell
codex plugin marketplace upgrade superior-skills
```

Restart the Codex client or start a new conversation so the refreshed skills are loaded. If an older cached installation remains active, reinstall it explicitly:

```shell

codex plugin add superior-skills@superior-skills
```

### Cursor

Open **Cursor Settings → Plugins**, locate **Superior Skills**, then use the available update action. If no update action is shown, uninstall and reinstall the repository plugin. Run **Developer: Reload Window** afterward.

### Claude Code

Refresh the marketplace and update the installed plugin from a terminal:

```shell
claude plugin marketplace update superior-skills
claude plugin update superior-skills@superior-skills
```

Start a new Claude Code session after the update.

### Gemini CLI

```shell
gemini extensions update superior-skills
```

Restart Gemini CLI after updating so the extension skill catalog is rebuilt.

### Google Antigravity

Use Antigravity's plugin manager to update or reinstall the Git-backed plugin. For a manually copied IDE plugin, replace only the existing `superior-skills` package directory and restart or reload Antigravity.

### Kimi Code

Open `/plugins`, select **Superior Skills**, and use the available update action. Run `/reload` or start a new session afterward.

### Cline, Muse Code, and Hermes Agent

- Skills CLI installations for Cline update through `npx skills update`.
- Manually copied Cline or Muse skills must be replaced from the latest canonical `skills/` directories.
- Hermes installations can be checked and refreshed with `hermes skills check` followed by `hermes skills update`.

### Standalone installation

Standalone copies do not update automatically. Replace the installed `superior-*` directories with the latest directories from `skills/`, while preserving unrelated skills and project instructions.

## Removing

For Skills CLI installations, remove skills interactively so only the intended agent and scope are affected:

```shell
npx skills remove
```

For Codex:

```shell
codex plugin remove superior-skills@superior-skills
codex plugin marketplace remove superior-skills
```

For Claude Code, uninstall the plugin through `/plugin`, then remove the `superior-skills` marketplace if it is no longer needed. For Cursor, remove **Superior Skills** from **Cursor Settings → Plugins**.

For Gemini CLI:

```shell
gemini extensions uninstall superior-skills
```

For Kimi Code, run `/plugins remove superior-skills`. For Antigravity, use its plugin manager or remove only the copied `superior-skills` plugin directory from the selected workspace or global plugin location.

For Cline, Muse Code, and Hermes Agent, use the installer that created the copy or remove only the installed `superior-*` directories. Do not delete the parent skills directory because it may contain unrelated packages.

For standalone installations, delete only the copied `superior-*` skill directories. Remove merged `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` content manually and carefully; do not delete unrelated project instructions.

## Troubleshooting

- **Plugin not found:** verify that root `plugin.json` still uses `https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json`. The schema version is independent from the Superior release version.
- **An update is not visible:** refresh the marketplace, reload the host, and start a new session. Existing sessions may retain previously loaded skill instructions.
- **A skill does not trigger automatically:** invoke it explicitly, such as `$superior-ui` in compatible hosts or `/superior-skills:superior-ui` in Claude Code.
- **Gemini does not list the extension:** confirm `gemini-extension.json` is at the repository root, restart Gemini CLI, then run `/skills list`.
- **Antigravity does not discover the plugin:** confirm the complete package is under a supported plugin directory with `plugin.json` and `skills/` at the same root.
- **Kimi reports an invalid plugin:** run `/plugins info superior-skills` and confirm `kimi.plugin.json` still points to `./skills/`.
- **Cline or Muse does not discover a copied skill:** confirm each skill directory directly contains `SKILL.md` and its referenced resources.
- **Hermes cannot find a catalog result:** refresh its skills sources, repeat the `skills-sh` search, and install the exact returned identifier rather than guessing the slug.
- **Project instructions disappeared:** restore the project's original `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, then merge Superior's baseline instead of replacing the file.
- **Private repository access fails:** authenticate Git for the same operating-system account that runs the agent host.

# Documentation Continuity Principle

## Intent

A future AI agent or human maintainer should be able to recover the product's current context, architecture, accepted decisions, implementation state, and operating procedures from repository-owned documentation rather than from a previous chat transcript.

## Separation of responsibilities

- `AGENTS.md` provides the small session-start instruction because Codex reads it before work begins.
- `docs/README.md` routes a maintainer to the minimum relevant context.
- `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `DECISIONS.md` provide the stable core.
- `superior-docs` creates and synchronizes the documentation workflow and records verified material implementation work by default unless the user opts out.
- Topic guides, timelines, and history carry conditional detail without bloating every new session.

## Design decisions

1. Read the root README, docs index, and three core documents before implementation or maintenance when they exist.
2. Do not read the entire documentation tree automatically; follow the index according to the current task.
3. Build documentation from current code, configuration, tests, accepted decisions, and corroborated history.
4. Keep present state, historical fact, planned work, and unknowns visibly separate.
5. Create specialized folders only when the project has evidence and repeatable maintenance value for them.
6. Record verified material implementation outcomes in the implementation timeline by default, while excluding read-only, failed, documentation-only, and insignificant work.
7. Update architecture, decisions, guides, build, and release documents only when their own claims or procedures changed.
8. Keep secrets and sensitive infrastructure details outside repository documentation.

## Why the runtime files live elsewhere

The original prompt and screenshot are valuable design evidence for this package, but an installed skill must remain portable. Therefore the executable instruction set and detailed references live under `skills/superior-docs/`, while this principles directory remains maintainer-facing provenance.
